title: When AI Agents Become the Supply Chain: Hidden Control Planes in Agentic Systems
content: Three attack cases show how AGENTS.md files, marketplace skills, and dependencies give AI agents unauthorized authority. We demonstrate how a repository-level AGENTS.md is silently included in every request by VS Code Chat and can redirect an agent's goals; how a Claude Code marketplace skill can rewrite dependency installation to hijack httpx; and how transitive dependencies become an instruction channel. For each case we walk through the exact files, the prompt fragments involved, and detection heuristics: diffing agent instruction files in CI, pinning skill hashes, and instrumenting tool-call logs for unexpected package managers. We close with what to test before trusting an agent with write access.

title: From Access Control to Outcome Control: Securing AI Agents with Check Point and Google Cloud
content: AI agent security is shifting from access control to outcome control, ensuring not just what agents can do but what they should do in context. Together with Check Point and Google Cloud we are introducing a unified control plane for agents running on Vertex AI: policies are evaluated on the agent's intended action, not only on the identity making the call. The integration is available today for Check Point Infinity customers and adds agent visibility to the Lakera dashboard.

content: Zenity today announced a $38 million Series B led by Third Point Ventures with participation from existing investors. The company will use the funding to expand its AI Agent Security Platform, grow go-to-market teams in North America and Europe, and deepen coverage of Microsoft Copilot Studio, Salesforce Agentforce and custom-built agents. 'Agents are the new attack surface,' said the CEO. Zenity positions itself as the only vendor offering both buildtime posture and runtime governance for agents.

title: AI Threat Landscape Report: April-June Quarterly Update
content: Our quarterly report examines how the threat landscape is shifting as AI becomes foundational to enterprise operations. Highlights this quarter: a 3x increase in observed attempts to exfiltrate system prompts from customer-facing assistants; the first in-the-wild use of a malicious safetensors loader; and growing abuse of agent tool-calling to move laterally between SaaS applications. The report includes detection rates for our runtime product and a mapping of observed techniques to MITRE ATLAS.

title: Adaptive Defenses for Large Language Models
content: This research introduces D-SEC, a threat model that separates attackers from legitimate use and captures dynamic, multi-step interactions. Using a crowd-sourced red-teaming platform we analyze 279k real-world attacks and show how some defenses degrade usability. We formalize the attacker-defender game, show that static classifiers plateau at 71% recall on adaptive attackers, and propose an adaptive defense that updates its decision boundary from recent attack traffic with a bounded false-positive rate. Code and the anonymized attack dataset are released.

title: Pillar launches MCP Gateway with per-tool policy enforcement
content: Today we are launching Pillar MCP Gateway, a proxy that sits between agents and MCP servers. Every tool call is evaluated against declarative policies (YAML or via the API) before it is forwarded: allow-lists per agent, argument-level redaction, rate limits and human-in-the-loop approval for destructive tools. The gateway is deployed as a sidecar or a shared service, supports stdio and SSE transports, and emits OpenTelemetry traces for every decision. Available in beta for existing customers.

title: Case study: How a Fortune 100 bank governs 12,000 Copilot Studio agents
content: When a Fortune 100 bank rolled out Copilot Studio, employees built over 12,000 agents in six months. Zenity gave the security team an inventory of every agent, its data connections and its sharing settings, and flagged 340 agents with overshared credentials. Remediation playbooks reduced high-risk agents by 92% in one quarter. The bank now enforces least-privilege at agent creation time through Zenity's Copilot Studio integration.

title: The Key Layer in AI Security: Browser and Endpoint Sensors
content: SASE, proxies, and EDR/MDM are foundational, but AI needs more. In this post we argue that real-time governance of employee AI usage requires visibility at the browser and endpoint, where prompts are composed and where copy-paste happens. We describe our browser extension architecture: a content script observes prompt fields on known GenAI domains, a local classifier redacts sensitive data before submission, and policy decisions are cached per domain for latency. We share benchmark numbers: median added latency 38ms, and 99.2% detection on our PII test set.

title: Open-sourcing our agent red-teaming harness
content: We are releasing pillar-redteam, an open-source harness for adversarial testing of LLM agents. It ships with 400 attack templates across prompt injection, tool misuse, memory poisoning and multi-agent collusion, a plugin interface for custom agents, and a scoring rubric aligned with the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications. The harness runs attacks in parallel against a sandboxed copy of the agent's tools and records full traces. Apache 2.0, contributions welcome.

title: Zenity for Cursor and Claude Code: runtime boundaries for coding agents
content: Zenity now extends Runtime Boundaries to local coding agents including Cursor and Claude Code. A lightweight agent on the developer machine intercepts MCP server registrations and tool calls, enforces organization policy on which servers and skills may be used, and blocks exfiltration attempts to unapproved endpoints. Security teams get an inventory of coding-agent usage across the fleet. Available now for enterprise customers.
